speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The construction time for each BTO project would vary based on the project’s attributes, such as the design complexity, the site conditions, the number of storeys.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: At each BTO sales launch, HDB would offer multiple housing projects at different locations, with different designs, flat types, prices and waiting times, to suit the varying needs of flat buyers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Because we do have a large group of different flat buyers with diverse needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This information is made available at project launch so that buyers can make considered decisions when they are applying for their BTO flats.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: And I thank the Minister for the reply.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I think most BTO projects do complete on schedule or even before schedule.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It is also in the interests of contractors to complete ahead so that they are able to recover and reinvest their capital faster.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, would the Ministry, perhaps, consider creating an incentive system for contractors, to reward them when they complete projects materially ahead of projections while maintaining quality standards?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It could be tax rebates or positive recognitions of their work.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Second, I received feedback from residents that in contrast to the recently newly announced and launched BTO developments which have much shorter waiting times, which is very much welcomed by residents, there are also some BTO developments, also in Yishun, that have a longer waiting time of around five to 10 years.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, some future homeowners now have a delayed life plans – whether it is starting a new family or moving into a new home.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, they are actually having a delayed life plans on that part.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, does HDB actually have measures to support or give recourse to these home buyers?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: And third, would the Minister consider allowing more plots of land, especially those that are projected to have longer development periods to start development ahead of the BTO schedule so that then they are able to then have a perceived shorter waiting time of flats for future time buyers?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: In other words, instead of Build-To-Order, we have Build-Before-Order, so BBO?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: My guidance to my colleagues in the Ministry of National Development and HDB is to build more and build faster so that we can keep up a robust supply of new HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It also helps with the re-allocation of resources across projects that the contractors are undertaking.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, HDB will indeed continue to work closely with the agencies and the contractors to expedite the approvals and to support timely project completion.
